subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Demographic Time Bombs
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Demographic Time Bombs.

hook.text: Japan's population shrinks by 800,000 per year. South Korea's fertility rate hit 0.72. Economies need people to grow.

buildup.text: Aging populations create economic risks: fewer workers, higher pension costs, lower growth, and strained healthcare.

discovery.text: By 2050, one in four people in Europe will be over 65. China's workforce will shrink by 200 million.

twist.text: Young populations in Africa create the opposite risk: rapid growth without enough jobs leads to instability.

climax.text: Demographics drive economics. Too old or too young — both create risks that take decades to develop and decades to fix.

punchline.text: Fertility rate 0.72. Population shrinking. No quick fix exists.

quiz.question: Why are aging populations an economic risk?
options: Fewer workers, higher pensions, lower growth, and strained healthcare
Aging populations have no economic effect
